newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil unions and Cosipa head in talks over strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil unions and Cosipa head in talks over strike.

text.p: The chairman of Brazilian steel company Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) was meeting stevedore union officials to resolve a labor dispute at the root of a strike at Santos port, an official said.
Aldo Narcise, chairman of the board of Cosipa, was meeting with delegates including Abelardo Fernandes, president of the National Stevedores' Union, said a spokeswoman for Cosipa.
But this was a personal initiative and the company's official line was that it was not meeting any stevedore representatives, she said.
"The board of Cosipa is not meeting anyone, the company's position is to only sit down to talk with the stevedores once they have a concrete position," the official said.
The reunion was taking place at the Sao Paulo headquarters of Companhia Paulista de Desenvolvimento, the firm which Narcise also heads, she added.
Workers at Santos began an indefinite strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT in protest against Cosipa using its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal at Santos.

The stoppage could spread to other Brazilian ports as early as Wednesday. Delegates of the National Stevedores' Union have yet to decide whether the strike should widen as a meeting scheduled to take place earlier was delayed, said the union's secretary-general Ernani Duarte.
